questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Zambia?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter L and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zambia article.

questions.proof: The capital of Zambia is Lusaka, which is also the largest city in the country.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Zambia?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter A and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zambia article.

questions.proof: It shares its borders with the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the north, Tanzania to the northeast, Malawi to the east, Mozambique to the southeast, Zimbabwe and Botswana (Via a very tiny border) to the south, Namibia (Via the Caprivi Strip) to the southwest, and Angola to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Zambia?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter E and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zambia article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Zambia is home to one of the seven natural wonders of the world, _____ falls.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter V and has 8 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Zambia article.

questions.proof: Zambia is home to one of the seven natural wonders of the world, Victoria falls.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It has had four democratic elections since _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the 90s of the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Zambia article.

questions.proof: It has had four democratic elections since 1991.
